name: Acer

project_scope.selection_mode: Four source-pool names; one installed canonical species, three comparison/source-pool concepts not installed by this lane
project_scope.important_status: A. palmatum is an East Asian ornamental; do not treat as native in project target zone. Source-pool curated flags are not canonical installed truth.
project_scope.learner_admission: Acer negundo canonical PASS; grandidentatum and saccharinum approved source-pool learner taxa, range UNRESOLVED.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: On a twig confirm OPPOSITE leaves; then look for a maple's PAIRED samaras, two one-seeded winged units attached at a common base. Separate compound leaves (A. negundo) from simple palmate leaves first. If palmate, flip a mature leaf: silvery underside versus not, and look for narrow V-shaped versus broad U-shaped sinuses.
shared_traits: Trees with opposite leaves; leaves can be simple and palmately lobed or pinnately compound (boxelder).
Fruit ordinarily a paired schizocarp of two winged one-seeded mericarps (samaras); intact pair is diagnostic relative to ash.
Small flowers and variable leaf lobing; juvenile leaves and cultivated selections can depart from expected shape.
shared_genus_recognition.guardrail: This is an identification lesson, NOT an installation or county-range certification for noncanonical species.

species_comparison_matrix.Acer grandidentatum: Simple palmate blade, usually 3–5 broad lobes
species_comparison_matrix.Acer saccharinum: Simple palmate blade, usually 5 sharply divided lobes (occasionally 3)
species_comparison_matrix.Acer palmatum: Simple palmate blade, typically 5–9 narrow pointed lobes

species_comparison_matrix.Acer negundo: Leaflet undersides green to somewhat paler; not dramatic silvery maple blade
species_comparison_matrix.Acer grandidentatum: Light-green to somewhat pale/glaucous, not striking uniformly silvery-white
species_comparison_matrix.Acer palmatum: Typically green beneath (or colored cultivars), not naturally strongly silver-white

species_comparison_matrix.Acer negundo: Not relevant: separate leaflets, not sinuses in one palmately lobed blade
species_comparison_matrix.Acer grandidentatum: Broad rounded U-shaped main sinuses, lobes broad, margins entire to weakly lobulate
species_comparison_matrix.Acer saccharinum: Very deep sharp V-shaped sinuses, central lobe often constricted at base
species_comparison_matrix.Acer palmatum: Deep narrow sinuses; usually 5–9 slender serrate lobes, cultivated variability considerable

species_comparison_matrix.Acer negundo: Individual leaflets often coarsely toothed or irregularly lobed
species_comparison_matrix.Acer grandidentatum: Broad lobes with relatively few large blunt teeth or secondary lobules
species_comparison_matrix.Acer saccharinum: Coarsely toothed lobes, long pointed tips
species_comparison_matrix.Acer palmatum: Usually sharp small serrations along narrow lobes, many cultivars highly dissected

species_comparison_matrix.Acer negundo: Deciduous riparian/bottomland tree, often confused with ash
species_comparison_matrix.Acer grandidentatum: Small–medium maple of limestone canyon/plateau settings; native status in target counties not set by this module
species_comparison_matrix.Acer saccharinum: Larger riparian and floodplain tree, also extensively planted; local origin must be separately checked
species_comparison_matrix.Acer palmatum: Small ornamental East Asian tree, often selected/cultivated; non-native comparison

species_comparison_matrix.Acer negundo: Paired samaras even though leaf resembles Fraxinus
species_comparison_matrix.Acer saccharinum: Paired samaras, often asymmetrical fruit pair
species_comparison_matrix.weight: GENUS CONFIRMATION; use timing and wing angle only with corroboration

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: mature node and leaf plus fruiting twig
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Opposite and compound, 3–5 separate leaflets + paired samaras → A. negundo candidate; if a single leaf is lobed, continue.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: underside of entire mature palmate leaf
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Strong, clear silvery-white underside and deeply lobed narrowed central lobe → A. saccharinum candidate.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: same leaf, central lobe and main sinuses with ruler
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Broad lobes, rounded U-shaped sinuses and modest teeth → A. grandidentatum candidate, including canyon/plateau contexts.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: thin lobes, serration, leaf underside and planting context
look_here_first_sequence.decision: 5–9 often sharply serrate narrow lobes, green undersides and ornamental provenance → A. palmatum comparison; cultivar forms may be highly variable.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: tree lacking reproductive characters or unusual landscape cultivar
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Keep Acer sp. and seek attached paired samaras + multiple mature leaf/twig views. Do not assign native-range status from nursery provenance.

scientific_cautions: Leaf opposite arrangement by itself does not distinguish Acer from ash (Fraxinus); fruit does: Acer paired samaras versus Fraxinus single samaras.
A. negundo is botanically a maple even though it has compound foliage. Do not misteach 'all maples have palmate leaves'.
A. grandidentatum and A. saccharinum pool records are marked curated in Sheets but have no separate species paths in the current canonical manifest; this genus lesson is not canonical installation.
A. palmatum is intentionally an East Asian/non-native horticultural comparison, not eligible for native-only counts merely from appearing in a source pool.
Cultivars and hybrid ornamental maples may alter tooth depth, colors or leaf dissection; use reproductive structures and accepted concept checks.
A. grandidentatum taxonomy includes regional variants; do not reassign native county decisions or split variants in this lesson.
A. negundo var. texanum is already represented at species level; do not create duplicate species for the infraspecific name.

local_lookalike_routing.separator: Opposite compound leaves as in A. negundo; inspect fruit — an individual single samara in Fraxinus versus joined double samaras in Acer.
Large palmate simple leaves may resemble maple but arrangement ALTERNATE, with hanging balls of achenes, not paired samaras.
Star-like lobed leaves arranged ALTERNATELY and spiny spherical infructescences, not paired samaras.

local_lookalike_routing.taxon: Acer rubrum (red maple, extra source-pool comparison only)
local_lookalike_routing.separator: Often 3–5 lobes with more angular V-shaped sinuses but undersides not striking silver as in A. saccharinum; compare teeth, bud and fruit.

look_here_first: Start with opposite nodes. Are leaves compound (A. negundo) or simple and palmately lobed? If simple, compare depth of sinuses and lower-surface color across several mature leaves.

comparison.saccharinum: Opposite simple, 3–5 lobes with deep V-shaped sinuses.

comparison.negundo: Not comparable: leaflets rather than lobes.
comparison.saccharinum: Often very deep, angular and narrow.

comparison.negundo: Variable leaflets; not a simple-maple separator.
comparison.grandidentatum: May be short-pubescent; not strongly silvery as a rule.
comparison.saccharinum: Conspicuously pale/silvery; may also have hairs.

comparison.grandidentatum: Paired samaras; use as confirmation, not sole split.
comparison.saccharinum: Paired samaras often maturing early; angle variable.

cautions: Acer grandidentatum synonyms under A. saccharum do not mean identical eastern sugar-maple concept.
Acer negundo is already canonical; this batch does not rewrite its species card.
Do not turn Texas state nativity into a project three-county PASS for either new species.
Fall leaf color, habit and fruit-wing angle alone are weak species characters.
